s6.saiNote: The Umrah guide has an animated walkthrough of sa'i.
doneNote: May it be an accepted Hajj, and may your sins be forgiven.
s5.li1: required for Tamattu' and Qiran. Most pilgrims buy an official voucher, and the animal is slaughtered on their behalf. Wait for confirmation before cutting your hair. If you cannot afford it, fast three days during Hajj and seven at home.
s6.li2: It is done like the Umrah tawaf, in wudu, seven counterclockwise circuits starting at the Black Stone, but usually in normal clothes, so there is no uncovered shoulder (idtiba) and no brisk walking (ramal).
s2.p: Hajj is Arafah. Being anywhere within its boundaries during this time is the one rite that, if missed, means Hajj is missed. Check the boundary signs; Masjid Namirah is partly outside it.
s1.li2: The same rules apply as in Umrah: no perfume, cutting hair or nails, hunting or marital relations; men do not cover the head or wear stitched clothing; women do not wear niqab or gloves.
s5.note: The sunnah order on this day is stoning, sacrifice, hair, then tawaf. The Prophet ﷺ allowed those who did them in a different order, so do not worry if crowds change your plan.
s3.li2: Collect pebbles about the size of a chickpea: 49 if you leave Mina on the 12th, 70 if you stay until the 13th. Taking a few extra is wise. They may also be picked up in Mina.
s7.li2: Each day after midday (zawal), stone all three jamarat in this order, seven pebbles each with takbir: al-Ula (small), al-Wusta (middle), then al-Aqabah (large).
s1.li1: In the morning, wherever you are staying in Makkah, bathe, wear ihram clothing and make your intention for Hajj. Qiran and Ifrad pilgrims are already in ihram.
qir.p: Enter ihram for Umrah and Hajj together and stay in ihram until the 10th. A sacrifice is required. The sa'i done after the arrival tawaf counts for Hajj.
s2.li3: Spend the rest of the day facing the qibla in du'a, dhikr, Qur'an and repentance, raising your hands. You do not need to climb Jabal al-Rahmah or see it.
s5.li3: after stoning and cutting the hair, everything forbidden in ihram becomes permitted again except marital relations. You may change into normal clothes.
heroLede: Five days, four places and eight rites, each shown as a moving diagram with the words to say, so you can see the whole pilgrimage before you begin it.
s7.tr1: "Whoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever delays, there is no sin on him, for the one who fears Allah" (2:203).
s4.li5: Someone who is unable, such as the sick or elderly, may appoint another pilgrim to throw for them after that person has thrown for themselves.
ifr.p: Enter ihram for Hajj only and stay in ihram until the 10th. No sacrifice is required. Like Qiran, sa'i may be done after the arrival tawaf.
s7.li3: After al-Ula, step aside, face the qibla, raise your hands and make a long du'a. Do the same after al-Wusta. Do not stop after al-Aqabah.
s4.li3: Throw seven pebbles one at a time, saying takbir with each. Each pebble must land in the basin; it does not need to hit the pillar.
s8.li2: Make it the last thing you do in Makkah. Buying a few things on the way out is fine, but staying on afterwards means repeating it.
s1.li4: Pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and the next Fajr in Mina, each at its own time. Dhuhr, Asr and Isha are shortened to two rak'ahs.
s7.li4: You may leave Mina on the 12th if you depart before sunset. Otherwise stay the night and stone again on the 13th.
s3.li4: Leave for Mina before sunrise. Women, the elderly, the weak and those caring for them may leave after midnight.
s5.li2: men shave the head (preferred) or shorten the hair evenly; women cut about a fingertip's length from the ends.
s2.li2: At Dhuhr time, pray Dhuhr and Asr together, both shortened to two rak'ahs, with one adhan and two iqamahs.
tam.p: Perform Umrah first and leave ihram, then enter ihram again for Hajj on the 8th. A sacrifice is required.
s3.svg: At night a pilgrim travels from Arafah to Muzdalifah, collects pebbles and leaves for Mina before sunrise
s2.tr1: The Prophet ﷺ said this is the best of what he and the prophets before him said on the day of Arafah.
s6.li1: This tawaf is a pillar of Hajj. It is best done on the 10th but may be delayed to the following days.
s4.li1: Only the large jamrah, the one nearest Makkah, is stoned today. Its preferred time is after sunrise.
s6.li3: Pray two rak'ahs, drink Zamzam, then perform sa'i: seven laps starting at Safa and ending at Marwah.
s3.li1: On arrival, pray Maghrib and Isha together, with Isha shortened to two rak'ahs, even if it is late.
s8.li4: If Tawaf al-Ifadah is delayed until departure, one tawaf with that intention can count for both.
s8.li1: Before leaving Makkah for home, perform seven circuits of tawaf al-Wada'. No sa'i follows it.
s3.li3: Sleep, pray Fajr early, then face the qibla and make du'a until the sky is bright.
s5.svg: The four rites of the 10th in order, and ihram restrictions lifting in two stages
s6.li4: Qiran and Ifrad pilgrims who did sa'i after their arrival tawaf do not repeat it.
s3.tr1: "When you pour down from Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram" (2:198).
s4.li4: Do not stop for du'a afterwards. If a pebble misses, throw another in its place.

s8.li3: Women who are menstruating or have postnatal bleeding are excused from it.

foot.p: This guide follows widely accepted practice for Hajj al-Tamattu'. Some details differ between schools of thought, such as the timing of stoning or what must be done in Muzdalifah, so check points that matter to you with a scholar or your group leader. Every pilgrim needs an official Hajj permit.
foot.fine: Diagrams are simplified and not to scale. Use the arrow keys or the numbered steps to move through the guide.
js.tStone: Circuit {n} of 7: face the Black Stone and raise your right hand.
js.tWalk: Circuit {n} of 7: walk with the Kaaba on your left. Make any du'a or dhikr you wish.
js.tYemeni: Circuit {n} of 7: between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone.
js.tFarewellEnd: Seven circuits complete. Pray two rak'ahs, then leave Makkah for home. May Allah accept your Hajj.
js.tIfadahEnd: Seven circuits complete. Pray two rak'ahs, drink Zamzam, then perform sa'i: seven laps from Safa to Marwah.
js.h10: 10th: stoning, sacrifice and hair in Mina
js.hIfadah: 10th: Tawaf al-Ifadah and sa'i in Makkah
js.c1a: Morning of the 8th in Makkah: bathe, put on ihram and make your intention.
js.c1b: Travel to Mina, reciting the talbiyah.
js.c1c: In Mina, pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha, each at its own time. Four-rak'ah prayers are shortened to two.
js.c1d: Spend the night in Mina and pray Fajr there.
js.c2a: After sunrise on the 9th, travel from Mina to Arafah.
js.c2b: At Dhuhr time, pray Dhuhr and Asr together, both shortened to two rak'ahs.
js.c2c: Face the qibla in du'a until sunset. This standing is the heart of Hajj.
js.c2d: At sunset, leave calmly for Muzdalifah. Do not pray Maghrib in Arafah.
js.c3a: After sunset, travel from Arafah to Muzdalifah.
js.c3b: On arrival, pray Maghrib and Isha together, with Isha shortened to two rak'ahs.
js.c3c: Collect small pebbles, about the size of a chickpea: {n} of 49, or 70 if staying until the 13th.
js.c3d: Sleep, pray Fajr early, then make du'a facing the qibla until the sky is bright.
js.c4a: On the morning of the 10th, walk to Jamrat al-Aqabah, the large one nearest Makkah. Stop the talbiyah.
js.c4b: Seven pebbles thrown. Do not stop for du'a here; move on to the sacrifice and cutting the hair.
js.c5a: Jamrat al-Aqabah stoned. Next comes the sacrifice.
js.c5b: Sacrifice: required for Tamattu' and Qiran, usually through an official voucher. Wait for confirmation that it is done.
js.c5c: Shave or shorten the hair. With stoning and hair done, the first release begins: change into normal clothes.
js.c5d: Go to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah and sa'i. After this, the ihram is fully lifted.
js.c5e: This is the sunnah order. Doing these rites in a different order is permitted.
js.c7a: After midday on the 11th, start at al-Jamrah al-Ula, the small one nearest the tents of Mina.
js.c7b: Step forward to the side, face the qibla, raise your hands and make a long du'a.
js.c7c: Walk on to al-Wusta, the middle jamrah.
js.c7d: Step to the side, face the qibla and make du'a again.
js.c7e: Walk on to Jamrat al-Aqabah, the large one.
js.c7f: Leave without stopping for du'a. Repeat on the 12th, and on the 13th if you stay.
js.rFirst: First release: all allowed except marital relations
